The SCP site is so big I haven't read it all, so I apologize if what I'm about to suggest is already ruled out by existing content, but I had an interesting thought to add after reading this page. I joined the site to share this.

It could be interesting if it turned out that the entities trapped inside each spear are actually antagonistic towards each other. The Scarlet King is powerful enough that in his presence they all shut up and obey, but when they are not in his presence each of them wants to be the one who gathers all the spears and uses them to bring the Scarlet King into this world. This infighting could be leveraged by humanity to fight against the bringing of the spears together.

I'll continue reading now and then, if this idea can be incorporated great, if not I understand that too. Thanks for the interesting content. :)

item.title: Re: Hello！ I have a question!
item.content:encoded:
It's a title in the organization. 'Minerval' was one of the three ranks in the original Bavarian Illuminati. I wanted to imply a similar hierarchy.

Minervan is derived from the name of the Roman goddess of wisdom. 'Illuminated' means 'enlightened' in this context, though it can also mean 'lit up brightly.'

item.content:encoded: As I said in my critique, the threat entity entry is far too long and big then what it needs to be. Threat entity files are supposed to be used/remembered in life-or-death situations, not in an academic/scientific setting like the foundation. You could probably remove a lot of the content from the entry (specifically the history and appendices) and make a PSYCHE or PHYSICS Records section, leaving the broad strokes in the Threat Entity section.

item.content:encoded:
Gonna voice my opinion regarding the longer sub-designations, since this is a suitable platform to discuss this.

IMO, I feel that codenames for GOC TEs should not be too long. Perhaps two codenames or two codenames and a suffix (e.g. '-child') will suffice. When there are three or more are present (i.e. the sub-designations here), it feels rather unwieldy for reading and feels too overly-complicated from the standpoint of a bureaucratic group and for a person talking about it. For instance, it would be a mouthful for field agents if they have to use overtly long names.

But of course, it did use Able, Bravo etc. to make things shorter. And I understand your usage of the codenames to imply that each spear has its specific powers.
